notes.message: The motherboard's firmware (ACPI) reserves the fan controller (it87 driver), so Linux won't drive it and motherboard fans are read-only (the BIOS keeps controlling them).
notes.guidance: Advanced, at your own risk: adding acpi_enforce_resources=lax to the kernel command line (GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT in /etc/default/grub, then update-grub and a reboot) lets the driver use the chip anyway. The firmware may be using the chip too, so readings or control can misbehave. NivaroOS never changes the kernel command line for you.
